html:
In 1471 the Vietnamese emperor Lê Thánh Tông invaded Champa and took its capital Vijaya, near today's Quy Nhơn in central Vietnam, ending Champa as a major power.

The Cham and the Vietnamese had fought for centuries along the coast. Thánh Tông led a huge army, and the chronicles report tens of thousands of Cham killed and captured, among them the king. The northern half of Champa was annexed, and what remained in the south broke into small princedoms under Vietnamese sway.

The conquest was the decisive step in the march to the south. Vietnamese farmers settled the central coast, and the Cham, whose temples stand at Mỹ Sơn, became a minority. Their last state was absorbed by the Nguyễn lords in the 1830s.
sum: In 1471 the Vietnamese emperor Lê Thánh Tông invaded Champa and took its capital Vijaya, near today's Quy Nhơn in central Vietnam, ending Champa as a major power.
